subject: Aircraft General Knowledge
question_text: What is the correct order of the strokes in a four-stroke piston engine?
explanation: The four strokes are induction (mixture drawn in), compression, power (combustion drives the piston down) and exhaust. They take two crankshaft revolutions.

incorrect_answer_explanations.B: The mixture must be drawn in before it can be compressed.
incorrect_answer_explanations.D: The cycle starts by drawing in the mixture.

question_text: During the power check, switching to a single magneto gives no rpm drop at all. What is the most likely cause?

choices.label: B
choices.text: The magneto's earth (grounding) lead is disconnected, so the magneto may stay live

explanation: On one magneto, combustion is a little less efficient, so some drop is expected. No drop suggests the switch is not grounding that magneto. It could then stay live with the switch OFF, a serious propeller-handling hazard.

incorrect_answer_explanations.A: A small rpm drop is normal on a single magneto; no drop at all is a warning sign.
incorrect_answer_explanations.C: Fouled plugs usually cause an excessive drop or rough running.
incorrect_answer_explanations.D: Carburettor ice reduces rpm generally; it is not checked by switching magnetos.

subject: Aircraft General Knowledge
question_text: In which conditions is carburettor icing most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Only at temperatures below -10 degrees C

choices.label: B
choices.text: Only at full power in dry air

choices.label: C
choices.text: High humidity at reduced power settings, with outside air temperatures well above freezing

explanation: Fuel evaporation and the pressure drop in the venturi can cool the induction air by 20 to 30 degrees C. In humid air, ice can form at outside temperatures up to about +30 degrees C, especially at low power (descent).

incorrect_answer_explanations.A: Very cold air holds little moisture; carburettor icing is common in mild, humid conditions.
incorrect_answer_explanations.B: Icing risk is greatest at low power, where the throttle valve is partly closed.
incorrect_answer_explanations.D: Carburettor icing can occur in clear, humid air.

learning_objective: Describe the effect of carburettor heat
question_text: Carburettor heat is applied when ice is present in the carburettor. What rpm indication is typical?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An immediate rise in rpm with no initial drop

choices.label: B
choices.text: A steady drop that never recovers

choices.label: D
choices.text: An initial drop in rpm, then a rise as the ice melts

explanation: Hot air is less dense and richens the mixture, so rpm first falls. As the ice melts, airflow is restored and rpm rises, often above the original value.

incorrect_answer_explanations.A: Hot, less dense air first reduces power, whether or not ice is present.
incorrect_answer_explanations.B: That is typical when no ice is present; with ice, rpm recovers as it melts.
incorrect_answer_explanations.C: Carburettor heat always changes the intake air density.

subject: Aircraft General Knowledge
question_text: Without adjustment, what happens to the fuel/air mixture as an aeroplane climbs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It becomes richer, because air density falls while the fuel flow stays about the same

choices.label: B
choices.text: It becomes leaner, because there is less fuel in the carburettor

choices.label: C
choices.text: It stays the same, because the carburettor compensates automatically

choices.label: D
choices.text: It becomes richer, because fuel density increases with altitude

explanation: The carburettor meters fuel by air volume. As air density falls with altitude, the mass of air per unit volume drops while fuel flow does not. The mixture becomes richer and should be leaned.

incorrect_answer_explanations.B: Fuel metering does not compensate for lower air density.
incorrect_answer_explanations.C: A simple float carburettor has no altitude compensation.
incorrect_answer_explanations.D: Fuel density is practically unchanged; the issue is lower air density.

question_text: Which condition makes detonation more likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Using a richer mixture than normal

choices.label: B
choices.text: Using fuel of a lower grade than specified

explanation: Detonation is the explosive, uncontrolled burning of the mixture. A lower grade (octane) of fuel than specified, a lean mixture at high power and high cylinder temperatures all promote it.

incorrect_answer_explanations.A: Extra fuel cools the cylinder and suppresses detonation.
incorrect_answer_explanations.C: Detonation is promoted by high temperatures.
incorrect_answer_explanations.D: Detonation is most likely at high power and high cylinder pressures.

question_text: An aeroplane with a fixed-pitch propeller enters a dive at a constant throttle setting. What happens to the rpm?
explanation: As airspeed rises, the angle of attack of the fixed-pitch blades falls and less torque is absorbed, so rpm rises. Pilots must watch for over-speeding.

incorrect_answer_explanations.A: Increasing airspeed lowers the blade angle of attack, so the propeller speeds up.
incorrect_answer_explanations.B: That would need a constant-speed propeller.
incorrect_answer_explanations.D: A fixed throttle does not change to idle by itself.

question_text: With a constant-speed propeller, what is the correct sequence to increase power?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increase manifold pressure first, then rpm

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increase rpm and manifold pressure at exactly the same time

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increase rpm first, then manifold pressure

explanation: To avoid high manifold pressure at low rpm, raise rpm before increasing manifold pressure. To reduce power, lower manifold pressure first, then rpm. Always follow the flight manual.

incorrect_answer_explanations.B: The standard technique sets rpm first.
incorrect_answer_explanations.C: With a constant-speed propeller both are set.

subject: Aircraft General Knowledge
learning_objective: Predict the ASI with a blocked pitot
question_text: The pitot tube and its drain hole become blocked by ice, while the static vent stays clear. How does the airspeed indicator behave in a climb?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It over-reads, increasing as altitude increases

choices.label: B
choices.text: It under-reads, decreasing as altitude increases

explanation: With pitot and drain blocked, the pressure in the pitot line is trapped. As the aeroplane climbs, static pressure falls, so the difference grows and the ASI reads higher. It acts like an altimeter.

incorrect_answer_explanations.B: Trapped pitot pressure stays fixed while static pressure falls, so the difference grows.
incorrect_answer_explanations.C: The ASI reads zero only if the pitot pressure falls to static, e.g. with the drain open.
incorrect_answer_explanations.D: A blocked pitot traps the pressure, so the ASI no longer reflects airspeed.

subject: Aircraft General Knowledge
learning_objective: Predict the ASI with a blocked static source
question_text: The static source becomes blocked at altitude while the pitot tube stays clear. How does the airspeed indicator read during a descent?
explanation: The trapped static pressure is lower than the true static pressure at the lower altitude. Pitot pressure, which includes the higher true static pressure, exceeds it by more than the dynamic pressure, so the ASI reads high. The altimeter freezes and the VSI shows zero.

incorrect_answer_explanations.A: Under-reading occurs in a climb with a blocked static source.
incorrect_answer_explanations.C: A blocked static source traps the old static pressure.
incorrect_answer_explanations.D: Pitot pressure is still supplied, so the needle does not drop to zero.

question_text: In an unpressurised aeroplane, the pilot selects an alternate static source inside the cabin. What is the typical effect on the altimeter?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It reads slightly lower than the true altitude

choices.label: B
choices.text: It freezes at the last indication

choices.label: C
choices.text: It reads slightly higher than the true altitude

explanation: Airflow over the cabin usually makes cabin pressure slightly lower than ambient. With that lower pressure, the altimeter and ASI read slightly high, and the VSI briefly shows a climb when the source is selected.

incorrect_answer_explanations.A: Cabin pressure is usually slightly below ambient, making the altimeter read high.
incorrect_answer_explanations.B: The alternate source supplies a working, if slightly inaccurate, static pressure.
incorrect_answer_explanations.D: Cabin pressure differs a little from outside static pressure.

subject: Aircraft General Knowledge
question_text: In the northern hemisphere, an aeroplane on an easterly heading accelerates. What does the magnetic compass indicate?

choices.label: B
choices.text: No error, because the heading is easterly

choices.label: C
choices.text: An oscillation only, with no directional error

explanation: Because of magnetic dip, the compass's centre of gravity is offset from its pivot. On east or west headings, acceleration swings the card to show a turn towards north and deceleration towards south (northern hemisphere).

incorrect_answer_explanations.A: In the northern hemisphere, deceleration on east or west headings shows a turn towards south.
incorrect_answer_explanations.B: Acceleration errors are greatest on east and west headings.
incorrect_answer_explanations.C: Acceleration produces a systematic error, not just an oscillation.

question_text: The ammeter shows a continuous discharge in flight, indicating alternator failure. What is the correct general action?

choices.text: Switch off the battery master to protect the battery

choices.label: B
choices.text: Continue normally; the battery will recharge itself

choices.text: Cooling, cleaning and helping to seal the pistons

question_text: What does an aircraft altimeter actually measure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The aircraft's distance above the ground by radar

choices.label: D
choices.text: Static (atmospheric) pressure, displayed as height using a standard atmosphere

explanation: Aneroid capsules expand as static pressure falls. The instrument converts pressure to height using the standard atmosphere, offset by the subscale setting.

incorrect_answer_explanations.B: Dynamic pressure is measured by the airspeed indicator.
incorrect_answer_explanations.C: The altimeter senses pressure; temperature causes errors.
